nodes.Name: asciiEqualFold
nodes.DocComment:
asciiEqualFold is strings.EqualFold, ASCII only. It reports whether s and t
are equal, ASCII-case-insensitively.

nodes.Name: lower
nodes.DocComment: lower returns the ASCII lowercase version of b.

nodes.Name: isASCIIPrint
nodes.DocComment:
isASCIIPrint returns whether s is ASCII and printable according to
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc20#section-4.2.

nodes.Name: asciiToLower
nodes.DocComment:
asciiToLower returns the lowercase version of s if s is ASCII and printable,
and whether or not it was.

nodes.Name: LowerHeader
nodes.DocComment:
LowerHeader returns the lowercase form of a header name,
used on the wire for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests.

nodes.Name: CanonicalHeader
nodes.DocComment: CanonicalHeader canonicalizes a header name. (For example, "host" becomes "Host".)

nodes.Name: CachedCanonicalHeader
nodes.DocComment: CachedCanonicalHeader returns the canonical form of a well-known header name.

nodes.Name: ErrRequestHeaderListSize
nodes.ValueLiteral: errors.New("request header list larger than peer's advertised limit")

nodes.Name: Request
nodes.DocComment:
Request is a subset of http.Request.
It'd be simpler to pass an *http.Request, of course, but we can't depend on net/http
without creating a dependency cycle.

nodes.Name: EncodeHeadersResult
nodes.DocComment: EncodeHeadersResult is the result of EncodeHeaders.

nodes.Name: EncodeHeaders
nodes.DocComment:
EncodeHeaders constructs request headers common to HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.
It validates a request and calls headerf with each pseudo-header and header
for the request.
The headerf function is called with the validated, canonicalized header name.

nodes.Name: IsRequestGzip
nodes.DocComment:
IsRequestGzip reports whether we should add an Accept-Encoding: gzip header
for a request.

nodes.Name: checkConnHeaders
nodes.DocComment:
checkConnHeaders checks whether req has any invalid connection-level headers.

https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9114.html#section-4.2-3
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113.html#section-8.2.2-1

Certain headers are special-cased as okay but not transmitted later.
For example, we allow "Transfer-Encoding: chunked", but drop the header when encoding.

nodes.Name: validPseudoPath
nodes.DocComment:
validPseudoPath reports whether v is a valid :path pseudo-header
value. It must be either:

  - a non-empty string starting with '/'
  - the string '*', for OPTIONS requests.

For now this is only used a quick check for deciding when to clean
up Opaque URLs before sending requests from the Transport.
See golang.org/issue/16847

We used to enforce that the path also didn't start with "//", but
Google's GFE accepts such paths and Chrome sends them, so ignore
that part of the spec. See golang.org/issue/19103.

nodes.Name: shouldSendReqContentLength
nodes.DocComment:
shouldSendReqContentLength reports whether we should send
a "content-length" request header. This logic is basically a copy of the net/http
transferWriter.shouldSendContentLength.
The contentLength is the corrected contentLength (so 0 means actually 0, not unknown).
-1 means unknown.

nodes.Name: ServerRequestResult
nodes.DocComment: ServerRequestResult is the result of NewServerRequest.
